problems.stem: A professional bio for a LinkedIn "About" section should usually be written in which voice, and why?
options: Third person ("Maria is a junior studying...") because it always sounds more formal.
First person ("I am a junior studying...") because LinkedIn is a personal profile where readers expect you to speak for yourself.
Second person ("You are reading about Maria...") to address the recruiter directly.
Whatever the AI tool chooses, since voice does not affect how a bio reads.
problems.explanation: A LinkedIn About section is your own profile, so first person reads as natural and direct. Third person is common for speaker bios or website team pages, but on a personal profile it can feel stiff or ghost-written.

problems.stem: A bio's first sentence reads: "I am a passionate, results-driven, detail-oriented self-starter." What is the main problem with this opening?
options: It is too short to be a real bio.
It stacks buzzwords that describe almost anyone and tell the reader nothing concrete about what you do.
It uses first person, which is wrong for a bio.
It should begin with your full legal name.
problems.explanation: Buzzword stacks ("passionate, results-driven, detail-oriented") are interchangeable across thousands of profiles. A strong opening names a role, a field, and one concrete thing you do.

problems.stem: You ask AI to draft your bio and it produces a polished paragraph describing "five years of industry experience leading cross-functional teams." You are a second-year student. What should you do?
options: Keep it; a confident bio gets more attention.
Keep the experience claim but change five years to three.
Rewrite it to reflect your actual level, such as coursework, a club role, and one project, and note the AI claim you removed.
Submit it as-is and explain in the interview that AI wrote it.
problems.explanation: A bio is a truthful self-description. AI happily invents seniority you do not have. Replace fabricated experience with real, level-appropriate detail and log what you removed.

problems.stem: Which bio opening best follows the pattern "who you are + what you focus on + one concrete proof"?
options: "I am a hard worker who loves to learn and grow every day."
"I am a CAT 100 student who is interested in many areas of technology and business."
"I am a sophomore studying management information systems, focused on data visualization; last semester I built an interactive sales dashboard in Tableau for a 30-person student org."
"My name is Jordan and I am currently a student at the university."
problems.explanation: The strong opening names the role (sophomore in MIS), the focus (data visualization), and one concrete proof (a Tableau dashboard for a 30-person org). The others stay generic or never get to evidence.
